messages:
sasha (eng-ml): heads-up: new upstream release 'phoenix-7b-lite' landed, license says "research only" + required attribution and a short model card URL. thinking about running it in sandbox for evals and doing a quantization experiment. any legal red flags?

liz (legal): quick read — "research only" usually = no commercial hosting or serving to paying customers. sandboxed evals for internal research + evals are typically okay, but we should not offer it via hosted API or Dedicated without an exception. need the exact license text to be sure. link?

sasha (eng-ml): paste: "Phoenix Public License v0.9: permitted uses — research and non-commercial experimentation; attribution required; redistribution of modified weights allowed only for non-commercial purposes." model card: https://models.example/phoenix-7b-lite/card

liz (legal): yup looks like non-commercial clause. two quick implications: 1) we cannot include it in the public hosted catalog or let trial credits hit it, 2) Dedicated/Private for paying customers is a no unless vendor grants commercial sublicense. For on-prem customer self-hosting, we can probably provide the tooling but not ship the weights ourselves.

oliver (infra): clarifying: for Dedicated we sometimes pull weights into our infra on behalf of customers (we'd be distributing). so that would trigger redistribution. For Private (customer-managed VPC) we can provide deployment tooling but cannot host or transfer the actual weights.

kevin (prod-eng): operational question — if we run quantized experiments and commit quantized checkpoints into our internal eval bucket (S3) for benchmarking, is that considered redistribution or just internal derivative?

liz (legal): internal derivatives used only for evaluation and not distributed externally are generally allowed under research-only, but keep access controls tight and document provenance. If we ever export those quantized weights to a customer or partner, that's redistribution and would violate the non-commercial clause unless we obtain permission.

sasha (eng-ml): noted. we'll gate the eval pipeline to a restricted bucket and mark all artifacts with provenance metadata. plan: run eval suite + quantization sweep (8-bit, 4-bit) and compare vs our baseline (raven13b) on benchmark set. eval-bot will kick off.

eval-bot: starting run: eval-runner --suite=llm_basics,qa,redwood_regress --model=phoenix-7b-lite --quant=none,8bit,4bit --output=sandbox/phoenix-20260305

oliver (infra): also flag: KV-cache format changes across quantized variants may make our runtime incompatible for fallback routing. if we find a quality regression post-quant, fallback to a compatible model must be configured.

kevin (prod-eng): let's add an A/B regression monitor: if quantized variant drops pass@k or increases hallucination rate beyond threshold, auto-disable that variant in canary routes.

liz (legal): one more thing — attribution. The license requires a visible attribution + link when the model is used. For internal eval UIs that's fine; if we ever present outputs externally (demo or hosted), we must include attribution text. Keep a checklist in model-onboarding doc.

sasha (eng-ml): will do. action items: 1) legal: confirm commercial exception process if needed. 2) infra: restrict artifact bucket and note redistribution rules. 3) eng-ml: run quant/evals and tag artifacts. 4) prod-eng: add regression gates for quant variants. will post results here. :white_check_mark:

liz (legal): I'll open a formal request template for a commercial sublicense if product wants to negotiate. cc @kevin.

kevin (prod-eng): cheers. once we have eval numbers we can decide whether to pursue. thanks all.
